question: is the exp014/exp016 disagreement on easy-class roots 17/19 (champion-local search crossed them, the uniform archive hybrid did not) archive DILUTION of the seed signal, or a root-lottery draw?
design: exact exp005 lane (targets 000/111, balance, n=3, train101/verify202/shots512, budget 6, restrict=('replace','indel')); exp006 skeleton birth [h(0),cx(0,1)]; exp015/016 archive regime (A1 verify_balance_bucket x length drives emission, A2 passive; fitness=train only, verify descriptor-only); TWO arms x roots 13/17/19: uniform (exp016 verbatim — deterministic replay per root, same rng stream; new draws come only from the rescue arm) + rescue (every 2nd emission parents from the single fittest A1 elite); lineage telemetry tracks birth-skeleton descendant survival per gen; 12 gens x pop 16
pre_run_pin: rescue crosses 17/19 below-bar-under-uniform = DILUTION VERIFIED (champion locality load-bearing); uniform replicates a new cross = LOTTERY DRAW (ARCHIVE NEUTRAL reinforced); both arms fail 17/19 w/ r13 control crossing = EASY CLASS DECOMPOSES (13 regime-robust, 17/19 champion-local-only rates)

results.verdict: EASY CLASS DECOMPOSES + RESCUE IS NOT A RESCUE: the uniform arm is a deterministic replay of exp016 (same rng stream per root — 13 crosses gen 4, 17 peaks 0.4355, 19 plateaus 0.2422, all byte-identical; the new signal is lineage telemetry, not new draws), and champion-rescue fails EVERYWHERE including the robust root 13 (max 0.4355) — bolting fittest-elite parenting onto the archive regime is actively harmful, so archive dilution is REFUTED as the 17/19 explanation and 'rescue' is not a mechanism. 13 is uniform-archive-robust; 17/19 remain champion-local-SEARCH-only crossings at measured rates (N/M doctrine, never mechanism victory)

honest_limits: The uniform arm is a DETERMINISTIC REPLAY of exp016, not a fresh sample: same lane, same archive regime, same rng stream per root (random.Random(root)) — r13 crosses at gen 4, r17 peaks at exactly 0.4355, r19 plateaus at exactly 0.2422, byte-identical to exp016. The replication confirms harness determinism; it adds NO new independent draws on that arm. The new evidence is (a) lineage telemetry and (b) the rescue arm's different rng stream (random.Random(root+1000)).

RESCUE IS NOT A RESCUE: bolting 50% fittest-elite parenting onto the archive regime LOWERS performance everywhere — the robust root 13, which crosses under the uniform archive in both exp016 and this replay, STOPS crossing under rescue (max 0.4355, below bar). Champion-local pressure inside a coverage-driven archive is actively harmful, not restorative. Archive dilution is REFUTED as the explanation for 17/19; 'just add champion pressure' is not a mechanism.

Root 13 is uniform-archive-robust (crosses at gen 4 twice, deterministic); roots 17/19 remain champion-local-SEARCH-only crossings at measured rates under every archive-regime arm tried (uniform, hybrid, rescue, transplant). Per exp012 ROOT-LOTTERY this is an N/M rate read per root, never a mechanism victory — the easy class itself decomposes (13 regime-robust; 17/19 champion-local-search-specific).
Roots 17's 0.4355 and 19's 0.2422 are NAMED at their measured values under both arms, never rounded up to the 0.45 bar.

results-style receipt (no witness LEDGER; exp001 remains the lane's only LEDGER receipt) — sealed artifacts are runner + results.json + telemetry jsonl, and the receipt's sha256 table must match every file byte-for-byte or the seal is void. The runner is sealed as the exact bytes executed in the qcells lab (workspace/labs/qcells).

The exp016 comparator is embedded with provenance (commit fba4ec7, PR #22 Casey-gated, NOT merged at seal time); if exp016's merged numbers ever disagree, this receipt's comparator pins must be re-audited, not silently trusted.

12 gens x pop 16 is the established archive budget, not an asymptotic sample; the rescue arm is ONE draw per root — a rescue-success rate on 17/19 is below this experiment's resolution, and the verdict does not claim one.
